name: explain_element
description: Why an element is in the export as it is, or is not in it: its provenance (with value_sources, the copy each reader took a value of its body from), its trust markers (the ...Source, ...Resolved and ...Refusal properties of its record) and every fail-closed decision recorded for it, each with a stage (element_skipped, body_not_drawn, body_left_as_box, opening_not_cut, outline_not_read, storey_not_bound), a reason code (the reason of the skipped item in get_diagnostics, or body_is_record_box, space_outline_is_record_box, area_body_refused, slab_shape_refused, wall_base_cut_refused, wall_end_extension_refused, wall_profile_extension_refused, saved_mesh_not_used), the stream and byte offset its record was read from where known, and a detail. Takes a Revit ElementId whether or not the export holds the element (a left-out element has decisions and no provenance), or the GlobalId of an exported one. The log keeps at most 5000 decisions a reason; capped_reasons names the reasons that dropped some, whose decisions about this element may be missing. A frame with no ElementId has no entry. Not read: family geometry, the Revit Mark parameter, and any body but the record's bounding box where provenance.body_source says so; see the summary's not_read and docs/status.md in the rvt-rs repository.

model.description: The `model_id` that `open_model` returned, or the path of the file.

element.description:
The element's Revit ElementId (`1234`), whether or not the export holds
it, or the 22-character IFC GlobalId of an exported one.

phase.description:
The project phase to read, by its name (exactly) or its ElementId,
instead of the project's last (`rvt-ifc --phase`). A phase named is
exact: naming the last phase differs from leaving `phase` out where the
last phase holds no room, since leaving it out then reads the rooms of
the latest phase that holds any. It applies to a file
path: a `model_id` names the phase its model was opened at. An unknown
phase is an error that lists the file's phases.

ElementProvenance.description:
Where one element's answer comes from. Every element in an answer carries
one. Fields the model does not have are absent.

element_id.description: The Revit ElementId, which the IFC export writes as the `Tag`.

global_id.description:
The IFC GlobalId the export writes: Revit's own where the file yields
it, otherwise one derived from the document's identity and the
ElementId.

category.description: The IFC entity the export writes, such as `IFCWALL`.

class.description: The Revit class the element's record names, such as `Wall`.

body_source.description:
How the element's body was derived, such as
`partition_element_record_bbox` (only its record's box) or
`partition_wall_centreline`.

profile_source.description: Where the plan profile of the body came from.

space_outline_source.description:
For a room or space, where its outline came from: `record_box`
(the area of its box, not of the room), `stored_solid`,
`stored_solid_faces`, `stored_solid_approximate`, `stored_solid_edges`,
`saved_mesh`, `family_body`, and for an Area `area_plan_topology`,
`area_plan_topology_unchecked` (which nothing outside the file checks:
Revit 2025 to 2027, and an Area drawn from lines whose partition copies
disagree), `area_boundary`, `area_boundary_joined` or `none`.

area_body_refusal.description: For an Area with no body, why it has none.

carrier.description: The kind of record the element was read from, such as `partition_element_record_first_prologue`.

stream.description: The stream the record is in: `Partitions/NN` or `Global/Latest`.

offset.description: Where the record or frame starts in that stream inflated: the frame the exporter selected (on Revit 2024 and later the greatest vertical extent, then the higher-numbered partition and later offset; on 2008 to 2023 the newest). A body reader may take another copy; `value_sources` names it.

record_offset.description: Where the ElementId is stored: the partition record header it is the first bytes of.

enclosing_record_id.description: For a frame inside another partition record, the ElementId of that record.

class_tag.description: The class tag the record names.

class_name.description: The class that tag resolves to in the file's own schema.

native_record.description: The element's native record, where the export's native passes indexed one.

provenance_omitted.description: True when the record fields are absent because the provenance table lists at most 250,000 elements and this one is past them (`file.omitted_entries`).

value_sources.description: The copy each reader took a value of the element's body from, where the reader notes it and the body is drawn from that reader (`body_source`): `get_element` and `explain_element` list them, `list_elements` does not. Absent for an element with no body of its own, and for one whose body is none of the kinds `docs/export-diagnostics.md` lists readers for.

NativeRecordOut.description: The native record the native readers hold for an element.

copies.description: In how many partitions the element has a native record.

copy.description: Which copy this is: `only`, `current` (the current one of several, RE-216) or `unresolved`.

stream.description: The partition of that copy, such as `Partitions/46`. It can differ from `provenance.stream`, the frame the exporter selected. The record a reader decoded is in `provenance.value_sources`, where that reader notes its choice.

offset.description: Where the record's header starts in that partition inflated.

class_name.description: The class the record names in the file's schema.

ValueSourceOut.description: The copy of an element's data a reader took a value from. The readers, the rules and what each source's `parts` are, are listed in `docs/export-diagnostics.md`, "Value sources".

reader.description: The name of the reader that took the value, such as the reader of a wall's location line or of a type's parameters. Each reader and the body it belongs to is listed in `docs/export-diagnostics.md`, "Value sources".

rule.description: How the copy was chosen. The rules are listed in `docs/export-diagnostics.md`, "Value sources"; for a source made of `parts` it is how each record's copy was chosen.

copies.description: In how many partitions the element's data named it, so how many copies there were to choose from; for a source made of several `parts`, how many records it is made of; for one record, in how many partitions that record was held.

stream.description: The partition of the copy, such as `Partitions/46`.

offset.description: Where the copy starts in that partition inflated: the element-data header whose element id follows it, for the readers of element data; the record's header, for a native record; the frame, for a body read from the frame.

partitions.description: Where every copy holds the same value, the numbers of the partitions that hold a copy; the copy named is the lowest-numbered partition's.

parts.description: The records the value is made of, where it is made of several or of another element's, at most 64. Such a source has no `stream` or `offset` of its own.

parts_left_out.description: How many more records than the 64 listed in `parts` the value is made of.

differs_from_frame.description: True when the value is held in another partition than `provenance.stream`, the frame: the copy named is in another and, where every copy holds the same value, so is every copy; for a source made of `parts`, none of them is in the frame's partition (`docs/export-diagnostics.md` says where a profile's records count as held there).

SourcePartOut.description: One record a value source is made of.

element_id.description: The ElementId of the record's element, which need not be the element the source is of.

stream.description: The partition the record is in, such as `Partitions/46`.

offset.description: Where the record starts in that partition inflated; what starts there depends on the reader.

DecisionOut.description: One fail-closed decision about an element (#1326).

stage.description: The step that made it: `element_skipped`, `body_not_drawn`, `body_left_as_box`, `opening_not_cut`, `outline_not_read` or `storey_not_bound`.

reason.description: The reason code: the `reason` of the `skipped` item in `get_diagnostics`, or `body_is_record_box`, `space_outline_is_record_box`, `area_body_refused`, `slab_shape_refused`, `wall_base_cut_refused`, `wall_end_extension_refused`, `wall_profile_extension_refused` or `saved_mesh_not_used`.

class.description: The class the diagnostics count it under: a Revit class, or an IFC entity such as `IFCDOOR`.

stream.description: The stream its record was read from, where known.

offset.description: The byte offset of the record in that stream inflated, where known. For the element-record reasons it is the element's last frame in scan order (partition number, then offset), which can differ from the frame `get_element`'s provenance names.

detail.description: What tells the reason apart: a phase's name, why an Area has no body, the `BodySource` of a box body.

FileProvenance.description: What the file itself says about where its elements come from.

revit_release.description: The Revit release that saved the file (from `BasicFileInfo`).

schema_class_count.description: How many classes the file's embedded schema (`Formats/Latest`) lists.

partition_count.description: How many `Partitions/NN` streams the file has.

layout_release.description: The release whose record layout the file takes, which can be older than the saving release.

omitted_entries.description: How many elements the provenance table left out past its cap of 250,000 listed; their record fields are absent and `provenance_omitted` says so.

ElemTableProvenance.description: How the file's `Global/ElemTable` stream frames its records.

record_stride.description: Bytes per record (28 or 40 on every file in the corpus).

owner_field_offset.description: Offset of the owner field within a record.

framing.description:
`explicit` for the 28- and 40-byte layouts, `implicit` for the
12-byte fallback no corpus file uses.

owner_field_bytes.description: Width of the owner field, on the explicit layouts.

exported.description: Whether the export holds the element. A left-out element has decisions and no provenance.

name.description:
The `Name` the export writes for the element, as in `list_elements`:
absent where the element is not exported, and for a room whose name is
exactly the exporter's `<class>-<ElementId>` placeholder.

provenance.description: Where the element's record was read from, where the export holds it.

trust_markers.description: Every `...Source`, `...Resolved` and `...Refusal` property of the element's record. Empty (`{}`) where the export has no record for it.

decisions.description: Every decision recorded for the element, by reason.

capped_reasons.description: The reasons whose log was full: a decision of one of these about this element may be missing.

file.description: The file the element comes from.

name: export_gltf
description: Write the model as a binary glTF 2.0 file to out_path, which must end in .glb, must not be the model, and must not exist unless overwrite is true. The file is the one rvt-gltf writes. If a resource limit kept part of the file unread, nothing is written unless allow_partial is true. Returns a summary (entity counts, unread streams, size and sha256) and a resource_link to the file; the glb is never returned inline. The entity counts are those of the IFC export: the glb also draws the pieces of elements of separate loops that the IFC folds into another element's body, and notes says how many. Sends progress notifications when the request carries a progress token, and cancelling it stops the export with nothing written. Writes only the file it is asked for. Not read: family geometry, the Revit Mark parameter, and any body but the record's bounding box where provenance.body_source says so; see the summary's not_read and docs/status.md in the rvt-rs repository.

model.description: The `model_id` that `open_model` returned, or the path of the file.

out_path.description:
Where to write the binary glTF. It must end in `.glb`, must not be the
model, and must not exist unless `overwrite` is true.

allow_partial.description:
Write the file even when a resource limit kept part of the model from
being read. The result lists the unread streams.

phase.description:
The project phase to read, by its name (exactly) or its ElementId,
instead of the project's last (`rvt-ifc --phase`). A phase named is
exact: naming the last phase differs from leaving `phase` out where the
last phase holds no room, since leaving it out then reads the rooms of
the latest phase that holds any. It applies to a file
path: a `model_id` names the phase its model was opened at. An unknown
phase is an error that lists the file's phases.

UnreadOut.description: A stream a resource limit kept from being read whole.

building_elements.description:
Building elements the IFC export writes (the diagnostics'
`exported.building_elements`), for `export_gltf` too: the glb also
draws each piece of an element of separate loops that the IFC folds
into the body of another element (`elements.folded_into_bodies`), which
is not counted here or in `entity_counts`, and `notes` says how many.

partial.description:
True when part of the file was not read and the export was written
anyway (`allow_partial`).

diagnostics.description: The export diagnostics (`ifc` only), as for `get_diagnostics`.

name: export_ifc
description: Write the model as IFC4 to out_path, which must end in .ifc, must not be the model, and must not exist unless overwrite is true. The file is the one rvt-ifc writes with the same switches (options); SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH fixes the time in its header. If a resource limit kept part of the file unread, nothing is written unless options.allow_partial is true. Returns a summary (entity counts, diagnostics, unread streams, size and sha256) and a resource_link to the file; the IFC is never returned inline. Sends progress notifications when the request carries a progress token, and cancelling it stops the export with nothing written. Writes only the file it is asked for. Not read: family geometry, the Revit Mark parameter, and any body but the record's bounding box where provenance.body_source says so; see the summary's not_read and docs/status.md in the rvt-rs repository.

IfcOptions.description: The `rvt-ifc` switches that change the model. The defaults are `rvt-ifc`'s.

revit_property_sets.description: Also write Revit's own parameter sets (`--revit-property-sets`).

revit_set_placement.description:
Also place properties where Revit's exporter does, and keep the
material it associates with an `IfcSpace`, which IFC4 does not allow
(`--revit-set-placement`).

allow_partial.description:
Write the file even when a resource limit kept part of the model from
being read (`--allow-partial`). The result lists the unread streams.

ModeArg.description: The quality the export must reach, as `rvt-ifc --mode`.

oneOf.description: Write what is recovered, however little (the default).
Require validated typed elements, and write no geometry.
Require at least one element with geometry.
Also require project metadata, units, levels and no warnings.

MeshesArg.description: Which bodies are drawn from the mesh Revit saved for display.

oneOf.description:
Every element that would be its record's bounding box, on Revit 2023 to
2027 (the default).

Doors and windows only, on Revit 2023 to 2027: the default before #1191,
and cheaper in time and memory.
Every element that would be its record's bounding box, on every release.
None: every element keeps its record's box.

model.description: The `model_id` that `open_model` returned, or the path of the file.

out_path.description:
Where to write the IFC4 file. It must end in `.ifc`, must not be the
model, and must not exist unless `overwrite` is true.

phase.description:
The project phase to read, by its name (exactly) or its ElementId,
instead of the project's last (`rvt-ifc --phase`). A phase named is
exact: naming the last phase differs from leaving `phase` out where the
last phase holds no room, since leaving it out then reads the rooms of
the latest phase that holds any. It applies to a file
path: a `model_id` names the phase its model was opened at. An unknown
phase is an error that lists the file's phases.

UnreadOut.description: A stream a resource limit kept from being read whole.

building_elements.description:
Building elements the IFC export writes (the diagnostics'
`exported.building_elements`), for `export_gltf` too: the glb also
draws each piece of an element of separate loops that the IFC folds
into the body of another element (`elements.folded_into_bodies`), which
is not counted here or in `entity_counts`, and `notes` says how many.

partial.description:
True when part of the file was not read and the export was written
anyway (`allow_partial`).

diagnostics.description: The export diagnostics (`ifc` only), as for `get_diagnostics`.

name: get_diagnostics
description: The export diagnostics of a model, as rvt-ifc --diagnostics writes them (docs/schemas/export-diagnostics.schema.json in the rvt-rs repository): what was decoded and exported, what was skipped, approximated or left out with the reason for each, unsupported features, warnings, the confidence level, and the streams a resource limit kept unread. What is not read: rvt-rs decodes a subset of a Revit file, and this server answers from the model the IFC export writes. An element's body is often only its record's bounding box (provenance.body_source says which); family files give no family geometry; an element's property sets hold the parameters the export writes, and Revit's own parameter sets need export_ifc with options.revit_property_sets; the Revit Mark parameter is not decoded; files saved by Revit 2015 to 2022, 2026 and 2027 are experimental, and 2008 to 2014 more so (release_support in the summary); get_diagnostics lists what the export skipped or approximated and why. docs/status.md in the rvt-rs repository (https://github.com/DrunkOnJava/rvt-rs/blob/main/docs/status.md) states what is read per release and category.

model.description:
The `model_id` that `open_model` returned, or the path of a `.rvt`,
`.rfa`, `.rte` or `.rft` file. A path that is not open yet is opened.

phase.description:
The project phase to read, by its name (exactly) or its ElementId,
instead of the project's last (`rvt-ifc --phase`). A phase named is
exact: naming the last phase differs from leaving `phase` out where the
last phase holds no room, since leaving it out then reads the rooms of
the latest phase that holds any. It applies to a file
path: a `model_id` names the phase its model was opened at. An unknown
phase is an error that lists the file's phases.

UnreadOut.description: A stream a resource limit kept from being read whole.

diagnostics.description:
The export diagnostics, as `rvt-ifc --diagnostics` writes them
(`docs/schemas/export-diagnostics.schema.json`).

name: get_element
description: One element, by Revit ElementId or IFC GlobalId (the Revit Mark parameter is not decoded, so it cannot be looked up). Returns its property sets and quantities as the IFC export writes them (quantities in the IFC's SI units), its trust markers (the ...Source, ...Resolved and ...Refusal properties of its record, such as BodySource), its name and long_name as list_elements gives them, its type object as the export writes it (element_type: the IFC entity as ifc_type, name and element_id, the type object's Tag, and the sets it holds; absent where the export writes none), its provenance (the carrier its record was read from, its stream and byte offset, and in value_sources the copy each reader took a value of its body from), and the file's: Revit release and build, schema class count, partition count and ElemTable record layout. Not read: family geometry, the Revit Mark parameter, and any body but the record's bounding box where provenance.body_source says so; see the summary's not_read and docs/status.md in the rvt-rs repository.

model.description: The `model_id` that `open_model` returned, or the path of the file.

id.description:
The element's Revit ElementId (`1234`) or its 22-character IFC
GlobalId, as `list_elements` gives them.

phase.description:
The project phase to read, by its name (exactly) or its ElementId,
instead of the project's last (`rvt-ifc --phase`). A phase named is
exact: naming the last phase differs from leaving `phase` out where the
last phase holds no room, since leaving it out then reads the rooms of
the latest phase that holds any. It applies to a file
path: a `model_id` names the phase its model was opened at. An unknown
phase is an error that lists the file's phases.

A body reader may take another copy; `value_sources` names it.

copies.description: In how many partitions the element's data named it, so how many copies there were to choose from; for a source made of several `parts`, how many records it is made of; for one record, in how many partitions that record was held.

name: get_summary
description: The summary open_model returns, for a model_id or a path: release and build, element counts by IFC entity and Revit class, levels, room count and the diagnostics summary (what was read, approximated, skipped and left unread). Element counts and lists are the elements the export writes: the further pieces of an element of separate loops, which it folds into the owner's body, are not rows and not counted (elements.folded_into_bodies counts them by IFC entity, as the diagnostics' exported.body_pieces_folded does). What is not read: rvt-rs decodes a subset of a Revit file, and this server answers from the model the IFC export writes. An element's body is often only its record's bounding box (provenance.body_source says which); family files give no family geometry; an element's property sets hold the parameters the export writes, and Revit's own parameter sets need export_ifc with options.revit_property_sets; the Revit Mark parameter is not decoded; files saved by Revit 2015 to 2022, 2026 and 2027 are experimental, and 2008 to 2014 more so (release_support in the summary); get_diagnostics lists what the export skipped or approximated and why. docs/status.md in the rvt-rs repository (https://github.com/DrunkOnJava/rvt-rs/blob/main/docs/status.md) states what is read per release and category.

The `model_id` that `open_model` returned, or the path of a `.rvt`,
`.rfa`, `.rte` or `.rft` file. A path that is not open yet is opened.

phase.description:
The project phase to read, by its name (exactly) or its ElementId,
instead of the project's last (`rvt-ifc --phase`). A phase named is
exact: naming the last phase differs from leaving `phase` out where the
last phase holds no room, since leaving it out then reads the rooms of
the latest phase that holds any. It applies to a file
path: a `model_id` names the phase its model was opened at. An unknown
phase is an error that lists the file's phases.

partition_count.description: How many `Partitions/NN` streams the file has.

layout_release.description: The release whose record layout the file takes, which can be older than the saving release.

omitted_entries.description: How many elements the provenance table left out past its cap of 250,000 listed; their record fields are absent and `provenance_omitted` says so.

ElemTableProvenance.description: How the file's `Global/ElemTable` stream frames its records.

record_stride.description: Bytes per record (28 or 40 on every file in the corpus).

owner_field_offset.description: Offset of the owner field within a record.

framing.description:

12-byte fallback no corpus file uses.

by_revit_class.description: By the Revit class the record names, such as `Wall`.

folded_into_bodies.description:

name: list_elements
description: List the building elements of a model, optionally by category (IFC entity such as IFCWALL), class (Revit class such as Wall) and level (storey name), paged by limit (100 by default, at most 1000) and offset. The rows are the elements the export writes, not the pieces it folds into another element's body (the summary counts those in elements.folded_into_bodies). Each row has the Revit ElementId, name and long_name (the IFC Name and LongName: an IfcSpace's are its room number (or <room name>:<ElementId> for a room with a name and no number) and its room name; name is absent only for a room with neither whose name is exactly the exporter's <Revit class>-<ElementId> placeholder, and the placeholder names of other elements are still served as name), level and a provenance object: element_id, global_id, category, class, body_source, profile_source, space_outline_source and area_body_refusal, and where the element's record sits: carrier, stream, offset, record_offset, enclosing_record_id, class_tag, class_name and native_record, each present only where the model has it. The rows leave out value_sources, the copy each reader took a value of the body from: get_element lists them. Not read: family geometry, the Revit Mark parameter, and any body but the record's bounding box where provenance.body_source says so; see the summary's not_read and docs/status.md in the rvt-rs repository.

name: open_model
description: Open a Revit file (.rvt, .rfa, .rte or .rft) and decode it once, with the same decode rvt-ifc runs. Every other tool answers from that decoded model and the IFC export is written from it, so an answer and the export cannot disagree. Handle lifetime: model_id is opaque and stays valid while this server process runs and the model is among the most recently used ones the server keeps (2 by default); after an eviction or a restart a tool returns an error and you call open_model again. Every tool also takes the file path in place of the model_id. Phase: pass phase (a phase name or ElementId) with the path to read a project phase other than the last, as rvt-ifc --phase does; the model_id then names that phase, and get_diagnostics lists the rooms it leaves out. unexported_element_records.description: Element records found but not exported for want of an ElementId.

notes.description: Steps of the export that were skipped or fell back, in words.

UnreadOut.description: A stream a resource limit kept from being read whole.

SkippedOut.description: Something the export left out or approximated, with how many.

count.description:
How many the reason counts. Mostly elements; for
`element_record_frame_stopped` it is frames of record markers in every
category (several frames can belong to one element), not lost elements.

model_id.description:
Opaque handle for the other tools. It lives while the server runs and
while the model is among the most recently used ones it keeps.

file_kind.description: `rvt`, `rfa`, `rte`, `rft` or `unknown`, from the file name extension.

revit_release.description: The Revit release that saved the file.

release_support.description: How the file's release is read, and that row's status.

room_count.description:
The number of `IfcSpace`s the export writes, of every kind: rooms, Areas
and family instances written as spaces. It is not the number of rooms
(the name is older than `space_kinds`); `space_kinds.room` is. On the
BIM4LCA office it is 308, of which 234 are rooms.

space_kinds.description:
The `IfcSpace`s by `RvtElementRecordGeometry.SpaceKind` (#1437): `room`,
`area`, `mep_space` or `family_instance`. The counts sum to `room_count`
less the spaces with no kind, which `get_diagnostics` counts as
`exported.spaces_without_kind`.

not_read.description: What the answers do not cover.
